K_problems.problem: 25 mandatory fields, and the form can't be saved part-way
K_problems.why: I can't answer Trade licence no., ISIC code, Budget or Data owner email from memory. I'd have to chase Finance, Legal and our DPO. If I can't save, I lose everything when I go to look something up. That's my first 45 minutes gone with nothing to show for it.

K_problems.problem: Mission*, Vision*, Risk appetite (1–10)* and Preferred methodology* are required
K_problems.why: I want ED waits down. I'm not writing our mission statement into a vendor form. 'Risk appetite' as a number would get quoted back at me in front of the board. And choosing the methodology is what I'm paying you to do.

K_problems.problem: Budget* is required with no 'none / opex only' option
K_problems.why: My constraint is no new capex. A required budget figure tells me you'll come back with a capex proposal.

K_problems.problem: Only one 'Data owner' field, and it doesn't reflect our approval chain
K_problems.why: Releasing patient data needs IT plus the DPO to sign off, which takes 2–6 weeks. There's no place to record that, no way to invite approvers, and nothing that shows a pending approval. The form assumes I can hand the data over myself, and I can't.

K_problems.problem: Jargon: 'EngagementSpec', 'EvidenceItems', 'M02 critical gaps', 'provenance class: observed', sales_tx, cust_master, mkt_spend_ts
K_problems.why: I don't know what any of that means. Worse, the gaps listed are sales transactions, customer master and marketing spend. Those are retail data, not ED arrivals, triage times or bed occupancy. It looks like a template that has nothing to do with a hospital, and I'd lose confidence immediately.

K_problems.problem: Red/green dots are the only status indicator, and the red one isn't explained
K_problems.why: I can't tell whether red means missing, rejected or overdue. And the dots wouldn't help a colleague with colour-blindness.

K_problems.problem: Drag-and-drop is the only way to upload, with no button
K_problems.why: Our locked-down hospital desktop may block it, and I'd expect a Browse button anyway. More importantly, I wouldn't upload patient-level data at all until the DPO approves. There's no route for de-identified or aggregate data, and no secure transfer handled by IT.

K_problems.problem: The only error is a 3-second toast saying 'Error 422: schema mismatch'
K_problems.why: It's gone before I've read it, and it doesn't tell me what's wrong or what the file should look like. If I'd got a file through IT and it failed, I'd have to go back to them with nothing to tell them. That's weeks wasted.

K_problems.problem: The session expires after 10 minutes of inactivity
K_problems.why: I get pulled into a bed-management call for 20 minutes and lose my work. Together with the no-save form, that's a guaranteed abandon.

K_problems.problem: Status screen shows only 'processing' and a spinner
K_problems.why: No timeline, no next step, no word on whether anyone at your end has looked at it. The CEO asks me 'when?' and I can't answer. I'd stop thinking of this as a serious supplier.

K_problems.problem: No sign of how data is protected, no human contact, no description of the report
K_problems.why: Before I commit anything I need to know where the data is held, who sees it and what the board will get. Nothing here tells me.

walkthrough: Day 0, about 5 min: I describe the problem in one box ('ED door-to-doctor median 2h40m, target under 1h, no new capex'). I don't upload anything because I'm not allowed to.
Day 0, about 8 min: answer 4 follow-up questions on the same page. Fine.

Day 1, about 3 min: email says a confirmation is waiting. 'What we understood' is good. I edit one line, swapping 'suspected cause: triage staffing' for 'boarding of admitted patients in ED', and confirm.

Day 1, about 15 min: the data checklist asks for ED attendance timestamps (Must have), bed occupancy (Must have) and rota (Helpful). Each item says why it's needed and how to get it. I click 'Someone else has this → invite them' and invite our Head of IT and the DPO. STUCK 1: I'm not sure whether the invitees can see the patient-level details, or what they're actually being asked to approve. I'd want a one-page data-protection summary (de-identification, where it's hosted, retention, a DPA template) that I can forward.

Day 1–30: waiting for DPO sign-off. The 'Your next step' card tells me 'Waiting on IT/DPO approval', which is good. STUCK 2: the checklist doesn't say whether the analysis could start on aggregate or de-identified data in the meantime. I'd ask, but I wouldn't give up, because the status keeps it alive.
Around day 32, 10 min: IT uploads the extract. One file fails, but the message says what's wrong and shows an example, so IT fixes it the same day.
Day 32–40: tracker moves through Analysis → Checking → Consultant review. The card says 'Results expected Thu'. Nothing needed from me.

Around day 40, about 40 min: I read the report. Answer in one paragraph, recommended steps, then 'How sure are we?' per finding. I ask about one Moderate finding. I download the Word version to put into our board paper format. STUCK 3: there's no board-ready executive summary, and nothing about the limitations or governance of using AI.
B.quote: This is the one I could live with for six weeks. I always know whose court the ball is in, and when the DPO holds us up it says so instead of just spinning. I'd still need a data-protection pack I can forward, and a version I can put in front of the board without rewriting.

walkthrough: Day 0, about 25 min: wizard step 1, company profile (6 fields), is easy. Step 2: I choose 'Operations' and describe the problem. Step 3: the suggested KPIs are generic, so I type 'ED door-to-doctor median' and 'LWBS rate'. Step 4: 'Constraints and budget'. I write 'no capex' and leave the budget at 0, and I'm uneasy about how that will be read. STUCK 1. Saving a draft helps, because I come back after a meeting.

Day 1, about 20 min: the data page is a table of required datasets with templates. Downloading the template is useful because I can send it to IT. STUCK 2: there's no 'someone else owns this' or 'awaiting approval' option. Status just shows 'missing'.

Day 1–30: the dashboard shows data completeness 0% and analysis 0% for four weeks. I can't tell whether it's waiting on me, my DPO or them. The CEO asks for an update and I've got nothing. STUCK 3. This is the point where I'd nearly give up, and I'd email the consultant directly.
Around day 32: IT uploads using the templates. Completeness reaches 100%. Charts start appearing on the dashboard but I don't know if they're final. STUCK 4: can I show these to anyone yet?

Around day 42, about 45 min: the formal PDF/Word report has an executive summary, methodology, findings and a confidence appendix. It's well structured for the board. The confidence information sits in an appendix, separate from each claim, so I have to cross-reference.
C.quote: The report itself I could hand to the board tomorrow. Getting there is a black box of percentages. Four weeks at 0% and I'd be on the phone asking whether anyone's actually working on it.

walkthrough: Day 0, about 15 min: I chat about the problem. Answering one question at a time is pleasant enough, though slow.
Day 0, about 3 min: the summary card is right, so I click [That's right].

Day 1, about 10 min: data requests come one message at a time. For each I either click [I don't have this] or have to explain in text that IT and the DPO must approve it. STUCK 1: I can't hand a request to IT or the DPO. I'd have to forward screenshots of a chat. My IT colleague isn't going to log into a chat thread.
Day 1–30: the waiting is a chat message saying 'I'm analysing', but it isn't analysing, it's waiting on my DPO. STUCK 2: to find what's still outstanding I have to scroll back up the thread.
Around day 32: IT gives me the files and I upload them in the chat. If one fails, the fix gets buried in the conversation. STUCK 3.

Around day 40, about 40 min: the report arrives as a long chat message. I download the PDF. STUCK 4: I'm not comfortable sending the board something that started as a chat transcript. I'd want to know what's a finding and what's chit-chat, and how sure you are about each finding isn't obvious.
Risk of abandoning: medium-high around week 3, when the thread is long and I can't see where things stand.
A.quote: It's friendly, but I'm not running a hospital project through a chat window. My DPO won't sign off on a chat, and I can't take a thread to the board.

interrogation.a: Being asked to upload patient data myself, or being made to feel I should get round our DPO. Second to that, weeks of silence with nothing but a spinner or 0%. If I can't tell the CEO where we are, I'll stop the engagement.
interrogation.b: Every number traced back to our own data, with the date range and how it was cleaned. A plain statement of how sure you are about each finding and why. Recommendations costed as zero-capex or opex-only, with the operational trade-offs (staff, beds, clinical risk). A named human consultant who signed it off. And a short pilot I can run in one ED shift pattern and measure in 4–6 weeks before I take it to the board.
interrogation.c: In B: (1) an 'Approvals' step in the tracker that names the IT/DPO approver and shows how long we've been waiting, plus a data-protection pack I can forward (DPA, de-identification, hosting, retention, who has access); (2) a path that starts with aggregate or de-identified data so work can begin while sign-off is pending; (3) a 'board version' export using a formal template: two-page executive summary, risks and limitations, confidence shown next to each finding, and a note on the AI method and human review; (4) limited access for the CEO or a board member so they can read but not edit.
interrogation.d: A 'start before patient data' mode. Analyse aggregate figures I can legally share today (hourly arrival counts, average waits, bed-occupancy totals) to produce a provisional view in week 1, which is then upgraded when the approved data arrives. Also a 'governance pack' generated automatically at the start for my DPO and IT. And after the report, a measure-the-pilot check-in so I can show the board whether waiting times actually fell.
